title: bmo's own answers
what: What bmo answers itself: the help listing every noun with its unit command and every unit the git rule reaches, the version, and the refusals for words and options it does not serve, in src/help.rs and src/answer.rs.

title: Command dispatch
what: The one run of bmo from its binary: the words read, the unit commands found and their nouns asked, the command resolved, and either a hand-over to the unit or an answer here, in src/lib.rs and src/main.rs.

title: Command hand-over
what: The hand-over: bmo becomes the unit command with every word in order and --via placed after the noun, so the unit's environment, streams and exit code stand for the run's, in src/hand.rs.

title: Home bridge client
what: A command whose declared noun carries the home mark, asked on a work node, is handed whole to the operations machine over the socket BMO_HOME_BRIDGE names, and its relayed output and exit code are the run, in src/bridge.rs.

title: Declared nouns and their cache
what: The nouns protocol: every unit command asked nouns with standard input closed and two seconds to answer, each line read as its words and marks, and the answers kept by path, size and modification time, in src/nouns.rs and src/cache.rs.

title: Command resolution
what: The order a command is resolved in: the longest declared noun the leading words match, a refusal where two unit commands declare it, the git rule of the first word, or nothing served, in src/resolve.rs.

title: Unit command discovery
what: The executables named bmo-<name> that bmo finds and hands commands to: the directory holding bmo first, then each directory of PATH, the first file of a name winning, in src/units.rs.

title: Command line reading
what: The command line as bmo reads it: --via, --help, -h and --version before the first word, and every word after it taken unchanged, in src/line.rs.
